score_method: Minimum mandatory visual-area score, not an average; every mandatory static visual check must pass strictly above 9.0.
pending_separate_evidence: Full GitHub byte/blob readback and independent archive gate
preservation: All previous source identities, original accepted images, rejected iterations and exact prompts remain preserved.

areas.finding: The golden/tan fictional Atlas Saber Wolf preserves the broad catlike snarling face, heavy tawny ruff, raised pale mane and long upper saber fangs. Its source label is retained; it is not substituted with a gray wolf or companion lion.
Front, rear, opposite left/right profiles and both obliques are distinct and fully framed. Native panel crops resolve the relevant facial, limb, tail and mane surfaces.
Four coherent quadruped limbs are resolved by the side and oblique views. Broad clawed paws contact the studio floor; no duplicated limb or floating foot is visible.

Two long upper saber fangs descend from the same mouth corners across front, profiles and front oblique. Short triangular ears, nose, cheek marks and one open jaw remain consistent; there are no extra tusks or horns.
One moderately short, thick furred tail attaches at the rump, with its pale distal tuft visible in profiles, rear and rear oblique.
Pale raised shoulder mane, tawny body, cream facial accents and dark claws remain stable. The reverse and oblique views resolve body volume without changing the source form.
Rounded sculpted masses, grouped fur, readable expression and restrained studio lighting match the approved Havenline static-reference presentation.

source_interpretation_limit: The small original Atlas source fixes visible identity. Hidden reverse anatomy and fine surface construction are authored static-reference interpretation. This approval establishes no native mesh, rig, animation, use state or gameplay behavior.
minor_polish_limit: Small fur-group contours and claw visibility vary with illustrative angle; major anatomy, facial markings, color distribution, tail length and saber-fang count remain consistent.
